analysis.investment_thesis: Nazara's 25.5% revenue CAGR superficially meets my growth threshold, but this is a capital-destructive acquisition roll-up masquerading as organic growth — net profit has actually declined at -2.7% CAGR over nine years. At 133x P/E and 100x EV/EBITDA with a 1.98% operating margin, the price demands perfection that the fundamentals cannot justify.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 25.5% over 9 years in India's fast-growing gaming/esports TAM
71% gross margins reveal strong unit economics at the product level — underlying IP has real value
Near-zero debt (D/E: 0.06) with ₹299 Cr cash preserves strategic flexibility for further acquisitions
key_risks: Acquisition-driven growth is destroying capital: equity ballooned from ₹501 Cr to ₹3,395 Cr (2020→2025) yet ROE is a paltry 2.9% — management is buying revenue, not creating value per share
Operating margin of just 1.98% means the consolidated business barely earns anything; 'Other Income' (₹80 Cr) nearly equals Operating Income (₹115 Cr), masking core operational weakness
Free cash flow turned deeply negative (-₹82 Cr) in FY25 alongside ₹1,139 Cr of investing outflows — the roll-up machine requires constant external capital, risking perpetual dilution
red_flags: Net profit CAGR of -2.7% over 9 years — growth in revenue and earnings must compound together; one without the other is hollow
Other Income (₹80 Cr) approaching Operating Income (₹115 Cr) — core gaming operations are barely profitable on their own
Massive equity dilution: total equity up 6.8x in 5 years with no commensurate improvement in returns — classic value-destroying roll-up pattern
EV/EBITDA of 100.8x is extreme even for a genuine hypergrowth company; this is not one
analysis.detailed_analysis:
My Scuttlebutt investigation of Nazara reveals a company that has confused acquisitive activity with genuine growth. Revenue CAGR of 25.5% looks compelling, but strip away the dozens of acquired entities — Animal Jam, Curve Games, Fusebox, SportsKeeda, Nodwin, PokerBaazi, and many more — and what remains is a fragmented portfolio of gaming and media assets generating just 1.98% in operating margins. The great growth companies I admire — the Motorolas and Texas Instruments of their era — built moats through innovation and organic expansion. Nazara builds by buying, and each acquisition dilutes shareholders: equity has grown 6.8x since 2020 while ROE sits at a dismal 2.9%. This is precisely the capital destruction that should alarm any growth investor.

The valuation compounds the problem. At 133x trailing P/E with forward P/E of 56x, the market is pricing in flawless execution of an unproven multi-vertical gaming roll-up across India, Africa, and the Middle East. Yet the FCF story is deteriorating — FY25 FCF was -₹82 Cr on ₹1,139 Cr of investing outflows. The financing machine (₹805 Cr inflow in FY25) must run continuously. I look for companies that generate their own fuel for growth; Nazara perpetually asks shareholders for more petrol. Unless management demonstrates it can convert this revenue engine into genuine earnings power — pushing operating margins toward 10%+ — this is a story stock at a story price, not the exceptional compounder my method demands.
